questions.question:
**In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Our soldiers sit in the top, (1)/ hold the ridge and can swiftly intervene, (2)/ as they pro-actively did in mid-June. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In part 1, the usage of an auxiliary verb is missing.
 
• The correct auxiliary verb should be 'can'.
 
• Here, 'Can' shows the possibility of the action {which is the main verb}.
 
• In the given sentence, the possibility is 'hold the ridge' and 'sit in the top'. 

**So the correct answer is-** *Our soldiers **can** sit in the top, hold the ridge, and can swiftly intervene, as they pro-actively did in mid-June.*

questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Earlier in June, Chinese troops (1)/have destroyed two of the old (2)/unmanned "self-help bunkers". (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**2**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419
a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The present perfect tense in part 2 is incorrect
 
• It must be replaced with **simple past **as the activity had taken place earlier.
 
• 'Have' will be removed and it will become **'Chinese troops destroyed two**...'.
 
• Correct sentence- *Earlier in June, Chinese troops destroyed two of the old unmanned "self-help bunkers". *

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

questions.question: A is younger than B, B is elder than C, C is younger than A, and D is elder than B. Who is the youngest among A, B, C, and D?

Hence, C is the youngest.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 7 and their product is 12. What is the sum of their reciprocals?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Sum of two numbers = 7

Product of two numbers = 12

**CALCULATION:**

Let, two numbers are x and y

Sum of these two numbers is 7

x + y = 7 ----(1)

Product of these two numbers is 12

xy = 12 ----(2)

Divide equation (1) by xy

x/xy + y/xy = 7/xy

1/y + 1/x = 7/12

∴ Sum of their reciprocals is 7/12

questions.question: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 200 which are not multiples of 4?
questions.solution:
Multiples of 5 from 1 to 200 can be represented as 5n, where n is any natural numbers and 1≤ n ≤ 40

∴ Number of Multiples of 5 from 1 to 200 = 40

5n will be a multiple of 4 if n is a multiple of 4

Now, multiples of 4 from 1 to 40 can be represented as 4m, where m is any natural number and 1≤ m ≤ 10

∴ Number of multiples of 4 from 1 to 40 = 10

∴ Required number = 40 - 10 = 30

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days and A alone can do it in 30 days. B alone can do the work in how many days?
questions.solution:
A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days

Part of work A and B can do in 1 day = 1/20

A alone can do the work in 30 days

Part of work A can do in 1 day = 1/30

∴ Part of work B alone can do in a day = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60

∴ B alone can do the work in 60 days

questions.question: If 2/5th of a cistern is filled in 6 minute, then what is the time needed to fill the remaining part?
questions.solution:
Given,

Part of cistern filled in 6 minutes = 2/5

Part of cistern filled in 1 minute = 2/30 = 1/15

∴ Total time required to fill the cistern = 15 minutes

Remaining part to be filled = 1 - 2/5 = 3/5

∴ Required time to fill the remaining part = 15 - 6 = 9 minutes

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio of 6 : 5. If the perimeter of the field is 132 metres, then what is its breadth?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ratio of Length and breadth of rectangle = 6 : 5

Perimeter of rectangle = 132 m

Formula used:

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b)

where l → length of the rectangle

b → breadth of the rectangle

Calculation:

The length and breadth are 6x and 5x respectively

Perimeter = 132

⇒ 2(6x + 5x) = 132

⇒ 11x = 66

⇒ x = 6

**∴ Breadth = 5 × 6 m = 30 m**

questions.question: A trader allows two successive discounts of 30% and 40% on selling an article. If he sells that article for Rs. 840, then what is the marked price (in Rs) of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Successive Discount = 30% and 40%

Selling price = Rs. 840

**Calculation:**

Let, marked price = Rs. x

After two successive discounts of 30% and 40%

Selling price

= x(1 - 0.30)(1 - 0.40)

= x × (0.70) × (0.60)

= 0.42x = 840

⇒ x = 840/0.42 = 2000

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 1050. A shopkeeper gives a discount of 30% and still makes a profit of 40%. What is the cost price (in Rs) of the article?
questions.solution:
Marked price = Rs. 1050

Discount = 30%

∴ Selling price

= 1050 × (1 - 0.30)

= 1050 × 0.70 = 735

Given,

Profit percentage = 40%

We know,

Profit percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

40 = [(735 - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

⇒ 0.40 × Cost Price = 735 - Cost Price

⇒ 1.40 × Cost Price = 735

⇒ Cost Price = 525

questions.question: If the price of a commodity is decreased by 40% and its consumption is increased by 30%, then what will be the percentage increase or decrease in the expenditure of the commodity?

1.30 numbers of units consumed in place of 1 unit

questions.question: A sum was invested on simple interest at a certain rate for 5 years. If the interest rate is increased by 2%, then the interest increases by Rs. 190. What is the sum (in Rs) invested?
questions.solution:
Simple interest = (P × r × t)/100

P = Principal

t = Time period

r = Rate of interest

Given,

t = 5 years

Let,

Principal = P

Rate of interest = r

Simple interest = (P × r × 5)/100 = Pr/20

After, increasing interest rate by 2% keeping amount of Principal and time fixed

Simple interest = [P × (r + 2) × 5]/100 = P(r + 2)/20

According to the question,

(Pr + 2P - Pr)/20 = 190

⇒ 2P = 20 × 190

⇒ P = 1900

questions.question: Who is the supreme law-making institution in India?
questions.solution:
• **Parliament is the supreme law-making institution in India.**
 
• It has two houses, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Parliament consists of the President and two Houses, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. 
 
 
• Parliament is the final authority for making laws in any country. This task of lawmaking or legislation is so crucial that these assemblies are called legislatures. Parliaments all over the world can make new laws, change existing laws, or abolish existing laws and make new ones in their place.
 
• Parliaments all over the world exercise some control over those who run the government. In some countries like India, this control is direct and full. Those who run the government can take decisions only so long as they enjoy the support of the Parliament.
 
• Parliaments control all the money that governments have. In most countries, and the public money can be spent only when the Parliament sanctions it.
 
• Parliament is the highest forum of discussion and debate on public issues and national policy in any country. Parliament can seek information about any matter.
 
 
 
• **President** is the head of the state and is the highest formal authority in the country.
 
• **Prime Minister** is the head of the government and actually exercises all governmental powers. He takes most of the decisions in the Cabinet meetings. The Prime Minister must have the support of a majority of Lok Sabha members.
 
• **The chief justice of India** is the chief judge of the Supreme Court of India as well as the head of the judiciary of India. The Chief Justice is, by law, the highest-ranking judicial official of India.

questions.question: What was the revenue system during Mughal emperor Akbar’s reign called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zabt System.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The revenue system during Akbar’s reign was called **Zabt System.**
 
• **Raja Todar Mal **was** Akbar's finance minister,** he introduced this system.
 
• He took a careful survey of crop yields and prices cultivated for a **10 years** period **1570-1580.**
 
• The system of taxation was called **Dahshala.**
 
• In this system, each province was divided into revenue circles with their own rates of revenue for each crop.
 
• On this basis, the tax was fixed on each **crop in cash.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Akbar was one of the mightiest emperors during the Mughal Era.
 
• He was born in October 1542 and died on 27th October 1605.
 
• Akbar was the third Mughal Emperor.
 
• His reign was between 1556-1605 AD.
 
• He was crowned in 1556, at the young age of thirteen years.
 
• He was assisted by Barram Khan.
 
• He is known for his liberal religious policies, relationship with Indian kings, conquests, etc.
 
• In 1564, he abolished the jizyah tax levied on non-muslims.
 
• Akbar introduced Mansabdari System in his administration.

questions.question: What is the season during the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is the summer season during the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The winter solstice is the day of the year that has the least daylight hours of any in the year.
 
• It usually occurs on 22 June but can occur between 21 and 23 June in the Southern Hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Summer Solstice

 
 
• It is the position of the Earth when the rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer.
 
• A large portion of the northern hemisphere experiences more heat and light. Hence, it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• In this position, the North Pole is tilted towards the Sun.
 
• During this period, days are longer than nights in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• It occurs on 21st June in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
 
 
• Winter Solstice
 
 
• It is the position of the Earth when the rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Capricorn.
 
• A large portion of the Southern Hemisphere gets light from the Sun. Hence, it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• In this position, the North Pole has tilted away from the Sun.
 
• During this period, nights are longer than days in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• It occurs on 22nd December in the Northern Hemisphere.
